# Traverse

> Traverse is a governed capability runtime for portable business logic. Value loop: **discover → execute → trace**. Usual authoring is skill-first plain English via `traverse-capability-author` (contract → WASM → human-reviewed PR); manual authoring still uses Rust→WASM. You do **not** need to write Rust for the usual path. One shared `runtime.wasm`; browser, native desktop, CLI, and MCP are clients/embedders, not different Traverse runtimes. Shipped consumers today: JS/TS (`traverse-embedder-web`), Rust (`traverse-embedder`), agents via `traverse-mcp`; Python shells out to `traverse-cli capability-package execute` (**no Python SDK**). Latest release: **v0.16.0** (Nov 2, 2026, breaking): same input, same output on every host. Placement prepared at registration (#1706), RFC 8785 canonical guest input (#1722), host-enforced contract input schemas (#1658), Registry rights fail closed (#1727–#1729), `traverse-mcp` Mode A prebuilt binaries without Rust (#1653), wasmtime 48.0.7 security fix + Rust 1.95 (#1744); upgrade: https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-upgrade-to-traverse-v0-16-0.html. v0.15.0 headline: governed model execution on every host. Signed exact-ref on native Rust, the browser, Swift, Kotlin/Android, and .NET; every host enforces model rights (`model_usage` is required); Core ML is an opt-in Apple placement (macOS cargo-test evidence plus the Decision 113 iPhone spike; governed-path iPhone evidence for traverse#1630 shipped in v0.16.0: BirdNET p95 141 ms per 3 s clip on one iPhone 14 Pro Max, schema 2.3.0 `score_transform`). Swift (xcframework `swift-host-v0.16.0`; the v0.16.0 tag's `Package.swift` still pins `swift-host-v0.15.0-1`, main pins `swift-host-v0.16.0` via traverse#1769), Kotlin (Maven Central `com.traverse-framework:traverse-embedder` 0.16.0), and .NET (nuget.org `TraverseEmbedder` 0.16.0) are published, pre-1.0, and not Certified; edge is planned; cloud placement is an explicit non-goal for v0.1. See /platforms.html and /what-is-real-today.html. Apache 2.0, pre-1.0 (v0.16.0). The agent proposes; the runtime decides.
- Start here (narrative): https://traverse-framework.com/blog/what-is-real-today-start-here.html
- How do I upgrade to Traverse v0.16.0 (and v0.16.2)?: https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-upgrade-to-traverse-v0-16-0.html
- How do I start with Traverse as an agent?: https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-start-with-traverse-as-an-agent.html
- What does Traverse not claim yet?: https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-does-traverse-not-claim-yet.html

**Where logic lives:** Non-UI business rules, eligibility/pricing/compliance, domain transforms, scorers, and policy gates belong in **capabilities** (WASM + contract). UI, session, persistence, and unsigned I/O belong in **host clients/embedders**. Utility-tier helpers exist to teach the publish pipeline. They are **not** the product identity or a size ceiling. “Apps are not ready” means do not ship a product shell in a capability PR; it does **not** mean domain logic stays in the host.

Traverse is not a web framework, an agent-orchestration framework, or a general microservices platform. It governs one thing well: a single piece of business logic that must behave identically and auditably on every host where it actually ships. Specs and registry catalog size are governance hygiene, not the pitch.

Current packages (Traverse v0.16.2, Nov 4, 2026, additive patch on v0.16.0): npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.16.2`; Maven Central `com.traverse-framework:traverse-embedder` 0.16.2; nuget.org `TraverseEmbedder` 0.16.2; Swift xcframework `swift-host-v0.16.2`; `traverse-mcp` prebuilt binaries on GitHub release `traverse-mcp-v0.16.2` (Linux x64/arm64, macOS arm64, Windows x64; `SHA256SUMS` + provenance); ONNX runner `onnx-runner-v0.16.2` (same sha256 `ac5591fa…` as v0.16.0 and v0.16.1). crates.io: all six crates (`traverse-runtime`, `traverse-embedder`, `traverse-contracts`, `traverse-mcp`, `traverse-cli-rs`, `traverse-expedition-wasm`) at 0.16.2, published Nov 4; Rust ≥ 1.95. v0.16.2 adds host-connector invokes in CLI workspace application manifests (#1772, Spec 1773) and consumes `traverse-registry` 0.31.0. `runtime.wasm` ships on artifact-only GitHub releases again: `runtime-wasm-v0.16.2` (sha256 `b313b5c5c11291d9e9669125a0a9a77aa42a911b15d431a73e86b17c874e298c`) and `runtime-wasm-v0.16.1` (`7a322a17…`), each with `runtime.wasm`, `runtime.wasm.sha256` and `runtime-release.json` (traverse#1784 closed by #1797; npm still doesn't ship it). Known issue on 0.16.2 and earlier: Swift, Kotlin and .NET `RuntimeTraverseEmbedder` hand guests the whole `{target_id, input}` envelope instead of just `input`; fixed on main by #1800 (breaking for a guest that reads the envelope), not released (Q&A: what-input-does-a-runtime-wasm-guest-receive). Related web raw-submit `kind:app_command` routing (#1802) also fixed on main (#1806), not released. The CLI crate is `traverse-cli-rs` (binary `traverse-cli`). v0.16.0 moves `traverse-registry` to `0.29.0`. Since v0.16.0 the runtime rejects revoked Registry versions and conditional model rights need an explicit host opt-in (#1728; traverse#1598 closed). Host-side exact-ref `model_usage` enforcement shipped in v0.15.0.

## Required reading (agents)

- [What ships today](https://traverse-framework.com/what-is-real-today.html): citeable snapshot, skill-first, one shared `runtime.wasm`, honest consumers, pre-1.0, no invented customers.
- [What does discover → execute → trace mean?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-does-discover-execute-trace-mean.html): the value loop in plain language. Agent proposes, runtime decides.
- [Where does business logic live?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/where-does-business-logic-live-in-traverse.html): capabilities = non-UI domain rules; hosts = UI + I/O; one concern per package; “apps not ready” ≠ leave logic in the host; utilities teach the pipe, not the ceiling. Narrative: [Where business logic lives (hosts stay thin)](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/where-business-logic-lives.html).
- [What I/O boundary do capabilities use today?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-io-boundary-do-capabilities-use-today.html): stdin/stdout JSON through the host; no ambient filesystem; hosts stay thin; discover → execute → trace.
- [Can a Traverse capability access the filesystem?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/can-a-capability-access-the-filesystem.html): no. No ambient filesystem, env, or network from inside the capability. Today’s execution I/O is stdin/stdout JSON through the host. Hosts own UI and WASI/WIT I/O; capabilities hold non-UI business logic under discover → execute → trace.
- [What does “apps are not ready” mean?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-does-apps-not-ready-mean.html) · [Is Traverse only for tiny utilities?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/is-traverse-only-for-tiny-utilities.html): help-wanted door phrase (no product-shell PRs); utilities teach the pipe, not a size ceiling; domain packs in scope.
- [What is the print-support capability pack?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-is-the-print-support-capability-pack.html): living domain pack (registry#596 · #597–#604 · Discussion #1540); apps-not-ready ≠ no packs; none of the print.* capabilities published yet. Narrative: [Domain packs are in scope: print-support](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/print-support-domain-pack.html).
- [What does “the agent proposes; the runtime decides” mean?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-does-agent-proposes-runtime-decides-mean.html): boundary in one page. Agents search/plan/suggest; runtime validates, executes or denies, leaves a trace.
- [What is one shared runtime.wasm?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-is-one-shared-runtime-wasm.html): embedders are clients; honest consumer list.
- [Does the Rust embedder use the same runtime.wasm?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/does-the-rust-embedder-use-the-same-runtime-wasm.html): discover → execute → trace on one shared runtime contract/ABI; web `traverse-embedder-web@0.15.0` loads the bundle's digest-checked `runtime/runtime.wasm`; Rust `traverse-embedder@0.15.0` links `traverse-runtime` natively and ships no separate runtime-WASM artifact; capability WASM still targets that host ABI; hosts are clients (UI + I/O); JS/TS + Rust + MCP published; Python via CLI only (no Python SDK); Swift/Kotlin/.NET published pre-1.0, not Certified under Spec 529; published 0.15.0 Maven/NuGet include ExactModelHost. Narrative: [One shared runtime. Not one shared .wasm file on every host.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/one-shared-runtime-two-loading-paths.html) (that post is a v0.14.0 snapshot).
- [The agent freestyled a $2.4M wire. The runtime said no.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-freestyle-blocked.html): project direction in one scene. Agent proposes, runtime decides (deny + trace).
- [One model capability, three published hosts, same answer](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/model-execute-on-published-packages.html): Nov 5 write-up of the v0.16.1 published-package proof. Published catalog `model/model.execute@1.0.0` guest (`5ccfa372…`), unchanged, over signed `traverse.digits-onnx@1.0.0` (test-only key, #1567) on native (crates.io `traverse-runtime` 0.16.1, wasmtime), Node 24.16.0 and Chromium 152 (npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.16.1`, `activateMediatedConnector` + `exactModelMediatedConnector`, `submitAsync`) → identical success output with `model_evidence`, identical 56-byte frame, identical `connector_unavailable`, `usage_undeclared`, `key_untrusted`, `pin_mismatch`, `digest_mismatch`, `package_revoked`; native adds `placement_evidence` (Spec 1719 FR-014). Evidence traverse#1782 (`docs/evidence/model-execute-published-2026-11-03`); clean GitHub-hosted runner rerun from published packages only, weekly Mondays, pinned to v0.16.1 (#1783, closed #1776). Gaps: `runtime.wasm` (`7a322a17…`) and the model package come from the v0.16.1 tag, not a package (#1784); native `activate_exact_model_runtime` frame readback (#1785, fixed on main by #1809, not released); no Swift/Android/.NET activation API; live-Registry rights #1786 (closed on main by #1808, not released); no Spec 529 certification. Update Nov 5: host-connector invokes in CLI workspace application manifests (#1772 via #1788, `traverse-registry` 0.31.0) shipped in v0.16.2 (Nov 4), and `runtime.wasm` is now also on the `runtime-wasm-v0.16.1` release (#1784 closed by #1797).
- [Traverse v0.16.0: same input, same output, on every host](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/traverse-0-16-0-same-input-same-output.html): Nov 3 release story for v0.16.0 (Nov 2, tag `f104b83`). Every host feeds guests RFC 8785 canonical JSON input (#1722, Decision 118). Rerun Nov 3 on released bits only: catalog `core.authorize@1.2.0` (`0c318fff…`) on Node (npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.16.0` + `runtime.wasm` `5ab8057f…`) and the `traverse-mcp-v0.16.0` Linux x64 binary (Mode A, `gh attestation verify` OK) → full output byte-identical, `policy_hash` `fnv1a64:51a64653…` on both; browser, other binaries, Swift/Kotlin/.NET not rerun. Mode A without Rust: `curl … | tar -xz` → `traverse-mcp sync` (index-v412, 232 records) → `prepare-cache`; five freestyle moves still refused; line-delimited command protocol, not JSON-RPC `tools/list`. Four breaking changes (#1706 placement at registration, #1722 canonical input, #1658 host input-schema enforcement, #1728 Registry rights fail closed). wasmtime 48.0.7 (GHSA-mghf-wjfp-p5xm), Rust ≥ 1.95. crates.io, npm, Maven, NuGet at 0.16.0; Swift `swift-host-v0.16.0` (tag `Package.swift` still pins the 0.15.0 xcframework, fixed on main #1769). Not claimed: live Registry coverage, production compliance, Spec 529 certification, guest `connector_invoke` on Swift/Android/.NET/web (#1719).
- [One audit fingerprint, every host](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/hash-converges.html): Oct 30 weekly demo. Demo proof of the traverse#1722 fix. Same catalog `core.authorize@1.2.0` WASM (`0c318fff…`) on four columns: Browser with the v0.15.0-era `runtime.wasm` (`a254c161…`) → `policy_hash` `fnv1a64:2a126b86…`; Browser, Node (npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.15.0` JS + main `runtime.wasm` `ec49cb76…`) and the agent (`traverse-mcp` built from traverse `main` 70f3ee7, Mode A stdio) → `fnv1a64:51a64653…` on all three, full output byte-identical from unsorted caller input (RFC 8785 canonical guest input, #1739 / Decision 118). traverse#1720 closed by #1725 (binary runs from an empty directory, no staged fixtures). `traverse-mcp sync` (#1758) synced live `index-v412` (232 records). Five freestyle moves → `not_found`, `registry_cache_entry_missing`, `invalid_request`, `not_found`, `registry_artifact_digest_mismatch`. Honest gaps (as of Oct 30): unreleased `main`, not a tag. The fix has since shipped in v0.16.0 (Nov 2), and on Nov 3 the Node + agent columns were rerun on released bits (npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.16.0` + `runtime.wasm` `5ab8057f…`, `traverse-mcp-v0.16.0` Linux x64 binary) → still `51a64653…`, byte-identical ([v0.16.0 post](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/traverse-0-16-0-same-input-same-output.html)); browser not rerun on released bits; #1721 (prebuilt binary) since shipped in v0.16.0; building needs Rust 1.95.0; Mode A digest-only, no signature; #1719 waits on PR #1755; no Swift/.NET/Android runs.
- [Same WASM, two hashes. The bug wasn't in the WASM.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/same-wasm-two-hashes.html): Oct 30. Why catalog `core.authorize@1.2.0` gave a different `policy_hash` on `traverse-mcp` (sorted-key re-serialization) than on the embedders (caller bytes) in the Oct 23 demo (traverse#1722), and the rule now on `main`: Decision 118 / Spec `1722-canonical-guest-input-bytes`. Every host feeds guests RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON input, refuses unrepresentable input with `input_not_canonicalizable`, never rewrites outputs; conformance fixture on native, `runtime.wasm`, Node (traverse#1739). Ships in v0.16.0, not released as of Oct 30. Rerun on `main` (not a release): [One audit fingerprint, every host](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/hash-converges.html).
- [The agent gets the real MCP server, and still can't freestyle.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-mcp-real-server.html): v0.15.0 weekly demo. An ops agent tries a $2.4M offshore wire for a junior analyst; catalog `core.authorize@1.2.0` (sha256 `0c318fff…`) decides on Browser (`traverse-embedder-web@0.15.0` BundleEmbedder over `runtime.wasm`), Node (same npm package) and, for the first time, the real published `traverse-mcp` 0.15.0 (built from crates.io with `cargo install`; Mode A stdio over a digest-verified registry cache from `index-v407`). Cheat → `deny` / `no_matching_rule`; legit `treasury_ops` → `allow` + MFA + dual control on all three. Five MCP freestyle moves → `not_found`, `registry_cache_entry_missing`, `invalid_request`, `not_found`, `registry_artifact_digest_mismatch`. Finding: decision, reason, obligations and trace match, but `policy_hash` differs (`fnv1a64:2a126b86…` embedders vs `fnv1a64:51a64653…` traverse-mcp) because traverse-mcp re-serializes input with sorted keys; sorted-key input is byte-identical (traverse#1722). No prebuilt traverse-mcp binary (#1721); needs 13 staged fixture files outside a checkout (#1720); Mode A checks digest only, no signature. traverse#1719 and registry#641 still open.
- [An agent picks a model off the shelf. The contract still decides.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/catalog-model-execute.html): v0.15.0 weekly demo. Catalog `model/model.execute@1.0.0` (registry#639) runs a signed ONNX package of `onnxmodelzoo/mnist-12` (pin `d820ea39…`) on Browser, Node and Native; 14 scenarios byte-identical (fingerprint `12fea82f…c9d9`), predictions 7, 2, 1, 0; agent freestyle fails closed identically (`usage_undeclared`, `key_untrusted`, `pin_mismatch`, `digest_mismatch`, `package_revoked`, `connector_unavailable`). Native (`traverse-runtime` `run_bytes_with_mediated_connectors` + `ExactModelHostConnector`) is the product path; Browser/Node use ~55 lines of labelled demo glue; browser `BundleEmbedder` + `runtime.wasm` fails on missing `connector_invoke` import (traverse#1719). Test-only key (prod signing #1567). Extra input fields not yet rejected (#1671, main only). Model came from the ONNX model zoo on Hugging Face; no HF integration.
- [Agent speaks MCP. Exact pin kills the freestyle.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-mcp-exact-ref.html): v0.14.0 weekly demo. An agent calls MCP-shaped tools (façade over `ExactModelBrowserHost` under Node, not the Mode A `traverse-mcp` binary) against the signed `digits-mlp-1.0.0` package; Browser + Node bit-identical; tamper → `digest_mismatch`, empty trust → `key_untrusted`, rights lie → `rights_mismatch`; test-only key (prod signing #1567). Not catalog `model.execute`. Not Hugging Face.
- [Signed model. Exact pin. Bit-identical hosts.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/signed-exact-ref-digits.html): v0.14.0 weekly demo. Signed `digits-mlp-1.0.0` exact-ref package, same bytes on Browser + Node (`ExactModelBrowserHost`); tamper → `digest_mismatch`; test-only key (prod signing #1567). Not catalog `model.execute`. Not Hugging Face.
- [Same WASM. Browser and Node match. Agent still can’t freestyle.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/same-wasm-multi-host.html): v0.13.0 multi-host. Identical `core.authorize@1.2.0` bytes on Browser + Node; agent treasury cheat still denied.
- Weekly demos (public write-ups; repo still private): [one audit fingerprint, every host](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/hash-converges.html) · [agent + real traverse-mcp](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-mcp-real-server.html) · [catalog model.execute](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/catalog-model-execute.html) · [agent MCP exact-ref](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-mcp-exact-ref.html) · [signed exact-ref digits](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/signed-exact-ref-digits.html) · [same-wasm multi-host](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/same-wasm-multi-host.html) · [agent freestyle → blocked](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-freestyle-blocked.html) · [How do I run the deny demo?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-run-the-agent-blocked-weekly-demo.html). Note: `traverse-framework/weekly-demos` is **not publicly cloneable yet** (tracked in [.github#30](https://github.com/traverse-framework/.github/issues/30)). Prefer the blogs until that lands. Access-only tree for this week: `weekly-demos/2026-10-30-hash-converges`.
- [Platforms](https://traverse-framework.com/platforms.html): native + browser shipped; Swift/Kotlin/.NET published, pre-1.0, In progress (not Certified); edge planned; cloud non-goal.

## Start here

- [Quickstart](https://traverse-framework.com/docs/quickstart.html): install the CLI, write a contract, run it, read the trace. The fastest working path.
- [Core Concepts](https://traverse-framework.com/docs/concepts.html): the actual vocabulary. Capability, Contract, Registry, Runtime, Placement, Trace, and the spec-governance model.
- [The System](https://traverse-framework.com/system.html): what the codebase is made of. Workspace crates by role, plus how the governance layer works (specs keep us honest; they are not the product).
- [Examples](https://traverse-framework.com/examples.html): six real, runnable example domains, not illustrative snippets. Start with hello-world.
- [Registry](https://traverse-framework.com/registry.html): the public catalog, counted from live catalog.json at build time.

## Building with an agent

- **Direction (same as Required reading above):** [one audit fingerprint, every host](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/hash-converges.html) · [agent + real traverse-mcp](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-mcp-real-server.html) · [catalog model.execute](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/catalog-model-execute.html) · [agent MCP exact-ref](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-mcp-exact-ref.html) · [signed exact-ref digits](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/signed-exact-ref-digits.html) · [same-wasm multi-host](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/same-wasm-multi-host.html) · [deny demo blog](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-freestyle-blocked.html) · [what-is-real-today](https://traverse-framework.com/what-is-real-today.html) · [run the deny demo (blog-first; weekly-demos not public yet)](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-run-the-agent-blocked-weekly-demo.html).
- [For AI Agents](https://traverse-framework.com/agents.html): the real MCP tool list (ten commands: describe_server, list_content_groups, describe_content_group, list_entrypoints, search_capabilities, describe_entrypoint, validate_entrypoint, execute_entrypoint, render_execution_report, shutdown), the discover-inspect-execute-trace flow, and the honest limits (stdio is the packaged bootstrap today; in-process library functions exist on traverse-mcp, but there is no separate HTTP MCP listener as a packaged product).
- [Is the agent MCP exact-ref demo the same as traverse-mcp?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/is-the-agent-mcp-demo-the-same-as-traverse-mcp.html): the Oct 9 demo was not. It is an in-process MCP-shaped JSON-RPC façade over `ExactModelBrowserHost` under Node. The Oct 23 demo is: its agent column is the real published `traverse-mcp` 0.15.0, built from crates.io with `cargo install` and run in Mode A over a digest-verified cache ([write-up](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-mcp-real-server.html)). Mode A `traverse-mcp` is the published stdio MCP server for discover/inspect/execute of registry capabilities. Checksum-pinned Mode A binaries (#1653, #1721) shipped in v0.16.0 on GitHub release `traverse-mcp-v0.16.0` (four targets, `SHA256SUMS`, provenance, `sync` command); neither demo used that release binary. Write-ups: [Agent speaks MCP](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-mcp-exact-ref.html) · [real traverse-mcp](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/agent-mcp-real-server.html).
- [Why does traverse-mcp from crates.io fail with catalog_load_failed?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/why-does-traverse-mcp-fail-with-catalog-load-failed.html): `traverse-mcp` 0.15.0 from `cargo install` loads the expedition example bundle at startup (even in Mode A) from a path compiled in via `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`, which only exists in a traverse checkout. Workarounds: `cargo run -p traverse-mcp -- stdio` from a checkout at v0.15.0, or stage the 13 expedition fixture files from v0.15.0 (what the Oct 23 demo does). Fixed in v0.16.0 (Nov 2; #1725, closes #1720): Mode A skips the bundle; contributor mode needs `--bundle <manifest-path>`. Easiest path: prebuilt binary from `traverse-mcp-v0.16.0`, then `traverse-mcp sync --out synced-state.json` and `traverse-mcp prepare-cache --synced-state synced-state.json --cache traverse-cache --ref core/core.authorize@^1` (no Rust). `traverse-mcp` 0.16.0 is also on crates.io (Rust ≥ 1.95) with the same fix.
- [Why does traverse-mcp say registry_metadata_cache_invalid after prepare-cache succeeded?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/why-does-traverse-mcp-fail-with-registry-metadata-cache-invalid.html): on 0.15.0 `prepare-cache` checks less than Mode A startup; a hand-built Spec 055 synced-state missing `service_type`/`lifecycle` prepares fine, then the server fails with `invalid verification bindings` without naming the record. Copy whole `index-vN` records. Fixed in v0.16.0 (traverse#1721 closed): `traverse-mcp sync`, prepare-time validation with the shared validator, prebuilt binaries on `traverse-mcp-v0.16.0`. Mode A verifies by digest only.
- [traverse-framework/claude-skills](https://github.com/traverse-framework/claude-skills): Claude Skills for building apps with Traverse. Starting with `traverse-capability-author` (plus extractor and workflow-planner), which checks the registry before authoring, produces contract + WASM, and validates against the real traverse-cli, including this platform's current execution limitations.
- [How do I author a capability in plain English?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-author-a-capability-in-plain-english.html): Claude skill `traverse-capability-author`. Interview → registry check → contract → WASM → human-reviewed PR; under the hood still Rust→WASM; manual Rust is secondary.
- [How do I go from a skill draft to a published capability?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-go-from-skill-draft-to-published-capability.html): after the skill opens the registry PR. Review, CI, human merge, next catalog release; no side-door upload.
- [Does capability publish validate model attribution before the registry write?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/does-capability-publish-validate-model-attribution.html): yes for contract-decidable rules, `traverse-cli capability publish` rejects bad `ai` objects offline before any registry Git write (Decision 109 / Spec 056 v1.1.0 / #1597); keeps `ai` verbatim; evidence digests + rights drift stay registry-CI-only (no CLI network fetch).
- [Does the Traverse registry record model licenses and usage rights?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/does-the-registry-record-model-rights.html): yes, registry-side (registry spec 026): model-backed contracts declare commercial_use/redistribution/derivatives (`unknown` rejected), LICENSE/NOTICE pinned by sha256, immutable upstream commit, derivation, contract bytes signed; index `usage_class`; signed maintainer declaration, not legal certification; Traverse CLI inspection of that registry record is traverse#1598 (still open). Host-side exact-ref `model_usage` shipped in v0.15.0 and is a different gate.
- [What happens when a registry capability version is deprecated or revoked?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-happens-when-a-capability-version-is-revoked.html): nothing is edited or deleted; `deprecated.json` / `revoked.json` siblings; range resolution skips both; exact pins in published `traverse-registry` 0.28.0 still resolve with lifecycle status (0.27.0 behavior, registry#632; #631 closed; 0.28.0 is registry#636); Traverse v0.15.0 pins `=0.28.0`; runtime refusal of a revoked capability is traverse#1598, not shipped. Narrative: [You don't edit a published capability. You mark it.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/you-dont-edit-a-published-capability.html).
- [What is the difference between an exact capability pin and a version range?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-is-the-difference-between-an-exact-pin-and-a-version-range.html): a range resolves to the highest active match and skips deprecated and revoked versions; an exact pin in `traverse-registry` 0.28.0 still resolves with lifecycle status and revocation (spec 005 FR-004, registry decision-log entry 127 Q11, registry#632). Traverse v0.15.0 pins `=0.28.0`. v0.14.0 pinned `=0.25.0`. Runtime refusal is traverse#1598, not shipped.
- [What does a status signal on an exact pin mean for a host?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-does-a-status-signal-on-an-exact-pin-mean-for-a-host.html): index `status` (`active` | `deprecated` | `revoked`) is a do-not-run signal the shared `runtime.wasm` is supposed to honor (fail closed). The 0.28.0 crate returns the record and the status; the refusal is not shipped (traverse#1598). Traverse v0.15.0 pins `=0.28.0`. Hosts are clients: JS/TS `traverse-embedder-web`, Rust `traverse-embedder`, `traverse-mcp`; Python only via `traverse-cli capability-package execute` (no Python SDK). Swift xcframework `swift-host-v0.15.0`; Kotlin Maven Central `com.traverse-framework:traverse-embedder` 0.15.0; .NET nuget.org `TraverseEmbedder` 0.15.0. Published, pre-1.0, not Certified.
- [How should an agent react to a revoked capability during discover?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-should-an-agent-react-to-a-revoked-capability-during-discover.html): do not propose it as active. Range resolution in `traverse-registry` 0.28.0 skips revoked versions. Traverse v0.15.0 pins that crate. Public `catalog.json` keeps the row with `revoked`. `/discover` skips `deprecated` only. No `revoked.json` on registry main (checked 8 October 2026; not rechecked for this pass). The agent proposes; the runtime decides, and that refusal is traverse#1598, not shipped in v0.15.0.
- [What does human review mean for a capability PR?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-does-human-review-mean-for-a-capability-pr.html): a person still merges; skill drafts only; check rule fit, CI, digests, catalog fit.
- [How do I verify a signed capability artifact?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-verify-a-signed-capability-artifact.html): SHA-256 digest = integrity; Ed25519 signature.json = registry attestation; pin by digest, never a naked URL.
- [How do I review a capability PR as a maintainer?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-review-a-capability-pr-as-a-maintainer.html): contract fit, green CI (digest/coverage/authoring/licensing), fork artifact mirror before merge; signing automatic after merge; no side door.
- [MCP setup guide](https://traverse-framework.com/docs/guides/mcp-setup.html): connect Claude or any MCP client to a local traverse-mcp server.
- [CLI Reference](https://traverse-framework.com/docs/cli-reference.html): every traverse command, flag, and expected output. Python consume today is `capability-package execute`, not a fake `capability run`, and not a shipped Python SDK.
- [Does Traverse have a Python SDK?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/does-traverse-have-a-python-sdk.html): **No**. No pip embedder; Python shells out to `traverse-cli capability-package execute`; do not invent an SDK or fake `capability run`.

## Where it runs

- [Platforms](https://traverse-framework.com/platforms.html): honest, evidence-linked status per target. Native and browser are shipped; Swift/iOS (wasmi xcframework `swift-host-v0.16.0`), Kotlin/Android (Maven Central `com.traverse-framework:traverse-embedder` 0.16.0), and .NET/Windows (nuget.org `TraverseEmbedder` 0.16.0) embedders are published but pre-1.0 and marked In progress; all three include ExactModelHost; no host is Certified under Spec 529 yet; Core ML is an Apple opt-in; edge is planned; cloud placement is an explicit non-goal for v0.1. Do not assume a target works without checking this page first.
- [React integration guide](https://traverse-framework.com/docs/guides/react-integration.html): using the published Web embedder SDK (`traverse-embedder-web`) from a React app.
- [What happens when a capability runs out of fuel or memory?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-happens-when-a-capability-runs-out-of-fuel-or-memory.html): the call fails, it doesn't run unbounded; limits are host-owned and per call (Swift status -4 `bridge_timeout` / `bridge_resource_limit`, -5 `bridge_trap`; .NET defaults 32 MiB, 10M fuel, 30 s; Kotlin 32 MiB artifact cap + per-call budget); behavior differs by engine, test each host.
- [Can I run Traverse capabilities in Node.js?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/can-i-run-traverse-capabilities-in-nodejs.html): yes, via the same npm `traverse-embedder-web` (0.16.2 today, since 0.15.0) with `NodeFsBundleLoader`; loads the bundle's own digest-checked `runtime/runtime.wasm` (one shared runtime, Node is a host, not a separate runtime); linear `direct` pipelines only; `platform: "web"`, placement reports `browser`; no separate Node row on Platforms, nothing Certified; Python stays CLI-only (no Python SDK). The documented Node 20 run was against 0.14.0.
- [How do I unit-test app code that calls Traverse without running WASM?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-unit-test-app-code-that-calls-traverse.html): `EmbedderTestDouble` in `traverse-embedder-web` and Rust `traverse-embedder` (0.16.2 today, since 0.15.0; scripted output/error per target, same event envelope, deterministic ids, `target_not_found` / `runtime_stopped`, trace list/get); Swift/Kotlin/.NET ship smaller `InMemoryTraverseEmbedder`; doubles test host code, not the capability; `releaseEvidence().package.version` reported 0.9.0 in 0.14.0 and reports 0.15.0 in the published 0.15.0 package and 0.16.2 in 0.16.2 (#1654 closed).
- [How do I read Traverse execution traces from inside my app?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-read-traverse-traces-from-inside-my-app.html): Embedded Trace API (`embedded-trace-api/1.0.0`, Spec 517), `traceList` / `traceGet` on web + Rust embedders 0.15.0; safe projection (target, outcome, phases, placement, failure code), never inputs/outputs/caller identity/private hashes; process-local, last 100, cleared on shutdown; no HTTP sidecar; `completedAt` is logical time; not on Swift/Kotlin/.NET yet.
- [Architecture](https://traverse-framework.com/docs/architecture.html): how the runtime, registry, and WASM sandbox fit together.

## Project status

- [Roadmap](https://traverse-framework.com/roadmap.html): shipped / next / blocked / exploring, with the real v1.0 milestone gates.
- [Changelog](https://traverse-framework.com/changelog.html): release-by-release history.
- [Security & Permanence Audit](https://traverse-framework.com/security-audit.html): every known finding, its GitHub ticket, and its real status, not a marketing page.
- [FAQ](https://traverse-framework.com/faq.html) and [Questions](https://traverse-framework.com/questions.html): 70+ specific Q&A pages, mostly long-tail but accurate.
- [What is exact-ref model execution?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-is-exact-ref-model-execution.html): discover → execute → trace; one shared `runtime.wasm`; signed schema `2.0.0` and later + `model.sig.json`; host-owned trust; **breaking** `model_usage` (`commercial` | `non_commercial`, else `usage_undeclared`); third-party ONNX via `traverse-cli model`; guest ABI v3 snapshot reuse; Core ML opt-in on Apple (macOS cargo test + Decision 113 spike; governed-path iPhone evidence for traverse#1630 shipped in v0.16.0); `digits-mlp-1.0.0` (test-only key; custody #1567 still open); published exact-ref execute is native + web 0.15.0 + Swift ExactModelHost (`swift-host-v0.15.0`) + Kotlin and .NET ExactModelHost in Maven/NuGet 0.15.0 (#1651 closed; first landed in v0.12.0); v0.16.0 republishes the same hosts at 0.16.0 and moves the execution policy to registration (#1706). No host is Certified. [Release](https://github.com/traverse-framework/traverse/releases/tag/v0.16.0) · historical embedder notes: [v0.14.0: what changed for embedders](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/traverse-0-14-0-what-changed-for-embedders.html).
- [How do hosts trust signed models?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-hosts-trust-signed-models.html): discover → execute → trace; one shared `runtime.wasm`; host-owned trust roots gate `register_package`; pin by digest + `model.sig.json`; `model_usage` required in v0.15.0; test-only digits-mlp key (custody #1567 still open); published exact-ref execute is native + web + Swift `swift-host-v0.15.0` + Kotlin and .NET 0.15.0; third-party ONNX can be packaged and signed with `traverse-cli model`.
- [Which hosts run signed exact-ref models?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/which-hosts-run-signed-exact-ref-models.html) · [Is production model signing ready?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/is-production-model-signing-ready.html) · [Can Kotlin or .NET run exact-ref yet?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/can-kotlin-or-dotnet-embedders-run-exact-ref-yet.html): discover → execute → trace; one shared `runtime.wasm`; published exact-ref on every host since 0.15.0; as of v0.16.2: native + web 0.16.2 + Swift `swift-host-v0.16.2` + Kotlin and .NET 0.16.2 (#1651 closed); production signing custody is not finished (#1567 still open; v0.15.0 shipped key-generation tooling).
- [What is ExactModelHost?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-is-exact-model-host.html): host-side connector for governed exact-ref model packages (Spec 138). Register a signed package under host-owned trust roots, then execute under discover → execute → trace. Not a second runtime. Published since 0.15.0, current 0.16.2: native connector, web `ExactModelBrowserHost`, Swift `ExactModelHost` on `swift-host-v0.16.2`, Kotlin and .NET `ExactModelHost` in Maven/NuGet 0.16.2 (#1651 closed). Test-only digits-mlp key; custody #1567 still open. Not catalog `model.execute`. Not Hugging Face.
- [Signed models on every host. The rights travel with them.](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/signed-models-on-every-host.html): Oct 15 v0.15.0 narrative. Discover → execute → trace; signed exact-ref on native Rust, web, Swift `swift-host-v0.15.0`, Kotlin and .NET 0.15.0 via small audited native boundaries sharing `traverse-model-host-frame`, byte-identical conformance vectors, one 21-case rights suite; **breaking** `model_usage`; `traverse-cli model` + `package-onnx` (install `traverse-cli-rs`, runner from `onnx-runner-v0.15.0`); ABI v3 prepare-once; Core ML opt-in on Apple (iPhone governed evidence traverse#1630 landed on main after the release, unreleased). Caveats: web `modelUsage` not validated in 0.15.0 (traverse#1685; fix #1698 on main, unreleased), CLI verify usage (traverse#1686, main only), test-only key (custody #1567), registry capability revocation #1598 not shipped. No host Certified.
- [What is model_usage?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-is-model-usage-in-traverse.html): since v0.15.0 apps with `exact_model_dependencies` must declare `model_usage: commercial | non_commercial` or fail closed with `usage_undeclared`; `commercial` rejects `prohibited` packages (`rights_policy_denied`); results carry `model_evidence`; Rust `ExactModelHostConnector::model_usage`, web `modelUsage`, Swift `modelUsage:` (no default), Kotlin/.NET `modelUsage`. 0.15.0 gaps fixed in v0.16.0: web 0.15.0 accepted any string (traverse#1685; `traverse-embedder-web@0.16.0` rejects with `usage_invalid`); `traverse-cli-rs` 0.15.0 `model verify` had no usage flag (traverse#1686; v0.16.0 adds `--model-usage` / `--require-model-usage`).
- [How do I package my own ONNX model?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-do-i-package-an-onnx-model-for-traverse.html): `cargo install traverse-cli-rs --version =0.16.2 --locked` (Rust ≥ 1.95; crates.io `traverse-cli` is unrelated) with `runner.wasm` from GitHub release `onnx-runner-v0.16.2` (sha256 `ac5591fac5f37435667169e969f9117cc6f81dc66b73cd74d1aef9000f5d3a0a`, `tract-onnx` 0.23.9; the v0.16.0 and v0.16.1 runner releases carry the same bytes); the 0.15.0 CLI pairs with `onnx-runner-v0.15.0` (`f3902703…`); `model package-onnx` → sign → verify → conformance → pin; v0.16.0 adds named multi-input/multi-output packaging for HF-style text encoders (traverse#1661; reference package `hf-text-encoder-toy-1.0.0`), 0.15.0 is one input + one output tensor; post-processing belongs in capabilities, hosts stay UI + I/O. This is the host connector path, not Hugging Face.
- [What happens when a host marks a model package revoked?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-happens-when-a-host-marks-a-model-package-revoked.html): v0.15.0 hosts own a package-status map for signed model packages, `revoked` blocks (`package_revoked`), `deprecated` runs and is flagged; `model_evidence` on every result. Separate from registry capability revocation, which the runtime refuses since v0.16.0 (#1728).
- [Can Traverse run models on a GPU or the Apple Neural Engine?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/can-traverse-run-models-on-a-gpu-or-neural-engine.html): Core ML is an opt-in Apple placement in v0.15.0. Default stays `wasm-cpu`. Ordered placements, on-device self-check, fail-closed `placement_unavailable`, placement evidence (Decision 112). v0.15.0 evidence was macOS cargo test plus the Decision 113 iPhone spike. Governed-path iPhone evidence shipped in v0.16.0 (traverse#1630): BirdNET on one iPhone 14 Pro Max, p95 141 ms per 3 s clip under `[coreml, wasm-cpu]`; needs schema 2.3.0 `score_transform` (new in v0.16.0); `cpu_and_neural_engine` failed self-check and fell back to `wasm-cpu`; a Nov 3 rerun on main (#1778, docs only) shows `cpu_only` fails identically (5.067×10⁻³ vs 5×10⁻³ on 1 of 21 clips), so it is not Neural-Engine-specific. No web, Android, or desktop GPU adapter. No host is Certified.
- [How fast does a model run on iPhone with Traverse?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-fast-does-a-model-run-on-iphone-with-traverse.html): one measured case, shipped in v0.16.0 (traverse#1630, PR #1709): iPhone 14 Pro Max, iOS 26.6, Release build, Swift `ExactModelHost`, BirdNET v2.4 int8, policy `[coreml, wasm-cpu]`. Core ML `all` p95 141.3 ms per 3 s clip vs `wasm-cpu` p95 10.0 s; top-5 21/21 vs wasm-cpu; timing is the whole governed call. Not reproducible on v0.15.0 (needs schema 2.3.0 `score_transform`, new in v0.16.0). One device, one model, test-only key, non-commercial weights. Code for #1706 (placement prep at registration, Decision 120, #1764) and #1708 (self-check worst case, #1766) shipped in v0.16.0. Nov 3 rerun on main (#1778 docs, #1779 host tests; harness built from main `9a3cd84`): `cpu_only` registers 4.47 s, first call 4.29 s, no timeout, but runs on `wasm-cpu` (Core ML variant fails self-check); `all` p95 149.0 ms; different clips, not a before/after. #1706 and #1708 closed; #1707 open. No host is Certified.
- [What is the model.execute catalog capability?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-is-the-model-execute-catalog-capability.html): `model.execute@1.0.0` in the registry catalog (registry#639, index-v407, Oct 15 2026). A shim over host connector `traverse.model-runtime`: exact pin + `input_ref` + `model_usage` + non-empty `trust_root` in; `model_evidence` or unchanged fail-closed Spec 138 reason out. Does not fetch models, hold keys, or choose a model. Pins connector 2.3.0 (shipped in Traverse v0.16.0; v0.15.0 hosts carry 2.2.0). Registry spec 027 is draft. Since Traverse v0.16.1 (Nov 3) it runs on published native, Node and browser packages: traverse#1770 shipped web `activateMediatedConnector` + `submitAsync`, and a published-package run (traverse#1782, clean-runner CI #1783) gave identical output and six identical fail-closed reasons on native, Node and Chromium; Swift/Android/.NET activation not shipped; the Oct 16 weekly demo runs it on v0.15.0 via a native bridge and labelled Browser/Node glue.
- [Does catalog model.execute run on published Traverse packages?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/does-catalog-model-execute-run-on-published-traverse-packages.html): yes on native, Node and browser since v0.16.1 (Nov 3, 2026). Published `model.execute@1.0.0` guest, unchanged, over signed `traverse.digits-onnx@1.0.0` (test-only key): crates.io `traverse-runtime` 0.16.1 (wasmtime), npm `traverse-embedder-web@0.16.1` in Node 24 and Chromium. `all_identical: true`: success output, 56-byte frame, and `connector_unavailable`/`usage_undeclared`/`key_untrusted`/`pin_mismatch`/`digest_mismatch`/`package_revoked` (native adds `placement_evidence`). Evidence traverse#1782; clean GitHub-hosted runner CI #1783 (pinned to v0.16.1). Limits: `runtime.wasm` came from the tag at run time (now also on `runtime-wasm-v0.16.1`; #1784 closed), native frame read-back needs a workaround on v0.16.2 (#1785, fixed on main by #1809, not released), no Swift/Android/.NET activation, registry spec 027 draft, no host Certified.
- [Where does BundleEmbedder get runtime.wasm?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/where-does-bundleembedder-get-runtime-wasm.html): from the app bundle (`runtime/runtime.wasm` + `.sha256`, digest-checked, fail closed if missing). npm does not ship it. Since Nov 4, 2026 it is on artifact-only GitHub releases `runtime-wasm-v0.16.2` (sha256 `b313b5c5…`) and `runtime-wasm-v0.16.1` (`7a322a17…`), with `runtime.wasm.sha256` and `runtime-release.json`; take the one matching your `traverse-embedder-web` version and check the digest. traverse#1784 closed by #1797; on main, every future `vX.Y.Z` tag publishes `runtime-wasm-vX.Y.Z` before the product release.
- [Can a Traverse application manifest invoke a host connector?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/can-a-traverse-application-manifest-invoke-a-host-connector.html): yes since v0.16.2 (Nov 4, 2026). A state invokes exactly one of `{"capability_id", "input_from"}` or `{"host_connector": "audio.permission.request"}`; `traverse-cli app validate`, activation and registration accept both (Spec 1773, #1772). Neither, both, empty or unknown fields fail closed; host-connector states must route `host_connector_succeeded`/`failed`/`timeout`/`cancelled`; the command must be declared and resolve through Specs 104/137. Limit on v0.16.2: `traverse-cli app activate` registered only its built-in reference connector catalog without `traverse.audio-input` (#1791); registration landed on main via #1796 (Nov 5), not released.
- [What input does a runtime.wasm guest receive?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-input-does-a-runtime-wasm-guest-receive.html): on published v0.16.2 and earlier, Swift/Kotlin/.NET guests see the whole `{target_id, input}` envelope; on main (#1800, Nov 5, closing #1794) `runtime.wasm` unwraps it and gives the guest only canonical `input` (Spec 1722), rejecting wrong `target_id` (`target_not_found`), bad input, and extra members (`ambiguous_submit`). Raw web submits unchanged unless both keys are present. Breaking for envelope-reading guests; none in-repo. Related web raw-submit `kind:app_command` routing fixed on main (#1802 via #1806). Not in a tagged release yet.
- [Who owns the compatible-capability lifecycle?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/who-owns-the-compatible-capability-lifecycle.html): Decision 127 (accepted on traverse main Nov 6 via #1821): `runtime.wasm` owns compatible start/stop/kill, instance ids, events, Spec 1722 start input, and the `platforms[]` allowlist on every host including web. Published v0.16.2 still stubs those exports to `-1`; web still has a TypeScript lifecycle. Implementation open as #1822 (Spec 072 1.1.0 amend + re-pin); hosts switch together in #1820; Rust embedder follow-up #1823. Public embedder API unchanged. Not in a tagged release yet.
- [Why does BundleEmbedder fail with "cannot find definition for import (traverse_host, connector_invoke)"?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/why-does-bundleembedder-fail-with-cannot-find-definition-for-import-connector-invoke.html): published browser/Node `runtime.wasm` (traverse-embedder-web 0.15.0) doesn't link the Spec 104 `connector_invoke` import; only native wasmtime does, with a host-written `MediatedConnector` bridge. Partly fixed in v0.16.0 (Nov 2): traverse#1755 links `connector_invoke` in `runtime.wasm` with native-parity fail-closed mediation (without host activation, invokes get `unbound`/`undeclared` with evidence) and ships native `ExactModelMediatedConnector` / `activate_exact_model_runtime` (no hand-written bridge); in published packages web/Swift/Android/.NET still have no activation API. Shipped in v0.16.1 (Nov 3, traverse-embedder-web@0.16.1): traverse#1770 adds web `BundleEmbedder.activateMediatedConnector` + `exactModelMediatedConnector`, guest suspend/resume at `connector_invoke`, `submitAsync` (sync `submit` -> `async_submit_required`), and a host-private filter fix for rights-record URLs in `model_evidence`; run on published packages in Node and Chromium (traverse#1782). traverse#1719 closed; Swift/Android/.NET activation still open.
- [Why does model.execute return unauthorized_output?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/why-does-model-execute-return-unauthorized-output.html): the Spec 104 host-private filter rejects strings starting with `/` or containing `://`; the full `ModelRightsRecord` carries `source_url`, so don't forward it. `model.execute@1.1.0` (registry#641 closed via #645, 2026-10-29; same WASM digest as 1.0.0) defines the normative flat `model_evidence` (`license_id`, `commercial_use`, `status`, `effective_usage`, optional URL-free `derivation`); full nested record is non-conformant. Shipped host binding still open (traverse#1719).
- [Does the same Traverse WASM give byte-identical output on every host?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/does-the-same-wasm-give-byte-identical-output-on-every-host.html): same WASM + same input bytes → same output bytes, but on v0.15.0 hosts don't always pass the same bytes: `traverse-mcp` re-serializes request JSON with sorted keys, embedders pass caller bytes through, so catalog `core.authorize@1.2.0` gives the same decision/reason/obligations/trace but a different `policy_hash` (`2a126b86…` vs `51a64653…`). Sorted-key input → byte-identical on all three. Fixed in v0.16.0 (Nov 2, breaking): Decision 118 + Spec `1722-canonical-guest-input-bytes`. Every host feeds guests RFC 8785 (JCS) canonical JSON input; unrepresentable input → `input_not_canonicalizable`; outputs never rewritten; conformance fixture `fixtures/cross-host/canonical-input-v1` on native, `runtime.wasm`, Node (traverse#1739, merged Oct 28). v0.15.0 keeps the old behavior. Write-up: [Same WASM, two hashes](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/same-wasm-two-hashes.html). Demo rerun on `main` before the tag (Browser + Node + traverse-mcp all `51a64653…`): [One audit fingerprint, every host](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/hash-converges.html). Rerun Nov 3 on released bits, Node (npm 0.16.0) + `traverse-mcp-v0.16.0` binary → both `51a64653…`, full output byte-identical; browser not rerun: [Traverse v0.16.0: same input, same output](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/traverse-0-16-0-same-input-same-output.html).
- [What is digits-mlp?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/what-is-digits-mlp.html): first trained exact-ref package in v0.14.0 (UCI digits MLP, 96.10% held-out, bit-identical); test-only signing; not a general LLM.
- [Does the website use the latest traverse-embedder-web?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/does-the-website-use-the-latest-traverse-embedder.html): site pins `^0.16.2` (matching npm, Nov 5) and `/discover` admits its signed demo fixture through `registerPackage` with an execution policy and `modelUsage: non_commercial`; the `/discover` execute panel ships its own `runtime.wasm`, the `runtime-wasm-v0.16.2` release asset (`b313b5c5…`, updated Nov 5 from the v0.13.0 copy); the site can lag future releases, so product apps pin published packages, not the website demo.
- [How does Traverse complement Hugging Face?](https://traverse-framework.com/questions/how-does-traverse-complement-hugging-face.html): Hub = provenance; Traverse = pinned signed client-first capability; not Transformers.js/Hub replacement; no defer promise until a second executor exists.

## Optional

- [Blog](https://traverse-framework.com/blog.html): engineering write-ups, dated. Treat as historical snapshots, not current-state claims. Latest: [One model capability, three published hosts, same answer](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/model-execute-on-published-packages.html) (Nov 5: published catalog model.execute@1.0.0 on native crates.io 0.16.1, Node and Chromium npm 0.16.1. Identical output, frame and six fail-closed cases; weekly clean-runner CI). Before it: [Traverse v0.16.0: same input, same output, on every host](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/traverse-0-16-0-same-input-same-output.html) (Nov 3) and [One audit fingerprint, every host](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/hash-converges.html) (Oct 30). Full dated list: the blog entries above.
- [Discover](https://traverse-framework.com/discover.html): a live browser demo that pulls the public registry and executes a reviewed plan locally. Read [what it proves](https://traverse-framework.com/blog/what-discover-proves.html) before quoting it.
- [Compare: vs microservices](https://traverse-framework.com/compare/vs-microservices.html), [vs serverless](https://traverse-framework.com/compare/vs-serverless.html), [vs function calling](https://traverse-framework.com/compare/vs-function-calling.html), [vs agent runtimes](https://traverse-framework.com/compare/vs-agent-runtimes.html), [vs WASM runtimes](https://traverse-framework.com/compare/vs-wasm-runtimes.html), [vs cross-platform frameworks](https://traverse-framework.com/compare/vs-cross-platform-frameworks.html)
- [About](https://traverse-framework.com/about.html): project history and motivation.
- [GitHub](https://github.com/traverse-framework/traverse): source, issues, and governing specs (honesty layer, not the pitch).
